w-es-013.title: Pa amb tomàquet (Bread with garlic & tomato)

instructions.1: Toast the bread slices under the broiler or on a hot grill for about 30 seconds per side.
instructions.2: Bring the toasted bread to the table. Give everyone a garlic clove to rub onto their toasted bread.
instructions.3: Rub the tomato halves on the toasted bread.
instructions.4: Drizzle with olive oil and season with salt and freshly cracked pepper to taste.
instructions.5: Serve warm.

w-es-013.culturalNotes: Pa amb tomàquet is a traditional Catalan dish served as an appetizer or light meal.

w-es-014.title: Alicante Style Patatas Bravas

instructions.1: Pre-heat your oven with the bake/broil option to its highest setting.
instructions.2: Finely mince 1 clove of garlic and 1 small dried cayenne pepper.
instructions.3: Heat a small saucepan over medium heat and add 1 tablespoon of extra virgin Spanish olive oil.
instructions.4: Once the oil gets hot, add the minced garlic and minced cayenne pepper, mix for 15 seconds, then add 1 cup of tomato puree, 1/2 teaspoon of smoked paprika, a pinch of white sugar, and season with sea salt and freshly cracked black pepper. Mix everything together and lower the heat to LOW.
instructions.5: Thinly slice 1 large Yukon Gold potato into rounds about 1/16 inch thick.
instructions.6: Arrange the potato slices on a baking tray lined with parchment paper in a single layer, drizzle each slice with a bit of extra virgin Spanish olive oil, and season with sea salt.
instructions.7: Place the tray in the oven and bake for 20 minutes until the potatoes are cooked.
instructions.8: Once the potatoes are cooked, place the slices in a serving dish, pour the tomato mixture over the potatoes, and garnish with fresh parsley.

w-es-014.culturalNotes: Patatas Bravas is a popular dish in Spain, especially in the Alicante region, where it is served as a tapa in bars and cafes.

w-es-015.title: Spanish Pisto Andaluz

w-es-015-i2.name: potato
w-es-015-i2.standardAmount: 1 medium potato (peeled and cut into small cubes)

instructions.1: Heat a large fry pan over medium heat and add the olive oil.
instructions.2: In the meantime, cut the potato into small bite-sized cubes.
instructions.3: Once the oil is hot, add the chopped potato and mix to coat them in the olive oil, then stir every 3-4 minutes to ensure even frying.
instructions.4: While the potatoes are frying, roughly chop the onion and garlic, finely chop the bell peppers and zucchini, and finely grate the tomatoes.
instructions.5: After frying the potatoes for about 20 minutes until they are golden brown, remove them from the pan and set aside, making sure to reserve the olive oil in the pan.
instructions.6: Using the same pan, lower the heat to medium-low, add the chopped onion, garlic, and bell peppers, mix together, then stir every 1-2 minutes.
instructions.7: After 6-8 minutes and the vegetables are lightly sautéed, add the chopped zucchini, mix together, then stir every minute or so.
instructions.8: Once the zucchini is lightly sautéed, about 4 minutes, add the paprika and cumin, quickly mix together, then add the grated tomatoes, the fried potatoes, and season with salt and pepper, mix together, then simmer for 5-10 minutes or until the grated tomatoes have slightly thickened.
instructions.9: Transfer the mixture to a large serving dish and garnish with fresh parsley, enjoy!

w-es-015.culturalNotes: Spanish Pisto Andaluz is a traditional Spanish dish served as a main or side dish, featuring a mix of sautéed and fried vegetables.

w-es-016.title: Rice Pudding

instructions.1: In a medium pot, bring the water to a boil.
instructions.2: Add the rice, salt, cinnamon stick, and lemon zest. Cover and simmer for 16 minutes or until the rice is tender.
instructions.3: In a large pot, add the milk and sugar and cook until the mixture is hot and the sugar dissolves when whisked.
instructions.4: Stir a few spoonfuls of the hot milk mixture into the egg yolks to temper them.
instructions.5: Add the tempered egg yolks back into the hot milk mixture and whisk to combine.
instructions.6: Add the cooked rice (with the cinnamon stick and lemon zest) to the milk mixture. Cook at a gentle simmer until thickened enough to stand a spoon up into it. This takes about 35-40 minutes.
instructions.7: Garnish with cinnamon, lemon zest, raisins, and slivered almonds.

w-es-016.culturalNotes: Rice pudding is a traditional dessert in Spain, often served on special occasions and family gatherings.

w-es-017.title: Spanish Potato Omelette

instructions.1: Peel the potatoes, wash them, and dry them with a cloth. Cut them into 1 cm cubes or 2 mm slices. Wash and dry them again. Add some salt to taste and mix them.
instructions.2: Heat the oil in a pan. When hot, fry the potatoes but do not let them get brown. Once they're done, drain the oil and store the potatoes.
instructions.3: Dice or slice the onion; fry it until it is translucent.
instructions.4: Beat the 8 eggs in a bowl with a small amount of salt until the mix is homogenous. Then, mix in the potatoes and the onion.
instructions.5: Heat 3 tablespoons of olive oil in an empty pan – you can use the previous pan after removing most of the oil.
instructions.6: Once the pan is hot, add the egg with the onion and the potatoes.
instructions.7: After 7-8 minutes, the bottom part should be done. Put the dish over the pan and carefully turn it around so that the undone part rests on the dish. This is the most difficult step of the recipe. After that, put the pan on the fire again and slowly slide the mix into the pan to cook the other side.
instructions.8: After a couple of additional minutes, it should be done and ready to serve.

w-es-017.culturalNotes: The Spanish omelette is a traditional dish in Spain, also known as 'tortilla de patatas'. It is usually served as a light meal or as part of a lunch.

w-es-018.title: Tarta de Santiago

instructions.1: Add 350 grams of blanched almonds to a baking tray lined with parchment paper and place it in a preheated oven at 170°C (340°F) for 8-9 minutes until the almonds are lightly toasted.
instructions.2: Remove the almonds from the oven and let them cool, then add them to a food processor and grind for 35-45 seconds until you get small chunks, not powder.
instructions.3: In a large bowl, mix 250 grams of granulated sugar with 5 large eggs, then add 1 teaspoon of cinnamon powder and 1 teaspoon of lemon zest, and mix well.
instructions.4: Gradually add the almond mixture to the egg and sugar mixture, and continue mixing until all ingredients are well combined.
instructions.5: Line a 9-inch (22 cm) round baking pan with parchment paper and spray the sides with nonstick cooking spray, then add the cake mixture to the pan and tap it a few times on the counter to release any air bubbles and level the cake.
instructions.6: Place the baking pan in the preheated oven at 170°C (340°F) and bake for 55 minutes until the cake is fully cooked.
instructions.7: Remove the cake from the oven and let it cool, then remove it from the pan and transfer it to a serving dish.
instructions.8: Place the Saint James paper cut-out cross on the cake and sprinkle with powdered sugar, then gently remove the paper cross and serve the cake.

w-es-018.culturalNotes: Tarta de Santiago is a traditional almond cake from Galicia, Spain, and is often decorated with the Cross of St. James.

w-es-019.title: Spanish Scrambled Eggs with Zucchini | Zarangollo Murciano

instructions.1: Crack 4 eggs into a bowl, season with sea salt and black pepper, and lightly whisk the eggs for about 10 seconds, leaving some streaks of egg whites.
instructions.2: Thinly slice 1/2 onion.
instructions.3: Peel 1 medium-sized zucchini and cut it into rounds about 1/8 inch thick.
instructions.4: Heat a large nonstick fry pan over medium-high heat and add 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil.
instructions.5: After 1 minute, add the sliced onion and mix with the olive oil. After 2 minutes, add the sliced zucchini and continue to mix. Cook for 5-6 minutes until the zucchini is translucent and developing a light golden color and the onions are caramelized.
instructions.6: Reduce the heat to low-medium, add the egg mixture, and mix every 30 seconds. Cook until the eggs form large chunks, about 3 minutes, or until fully cooked. Remove the pan from the heat.
instructions.7: Transfer the mixture to a serving dish and sprinkle with freshly chopped chives. Enjoy!

w-es-019.culturalNotes: Zarangollo Murciano is a traditional dish from the Murcia region in Spain, known for its simplicity and rich flavor.

w-kr-001.title: Dol Sot Bibimbap (Korean Rice Dish)

instructions.1: Combine soy sauce, white sugar, brown sugar, minced garlic, chopped green onion, and toasted sesame seeds in a large bowl. Add sliced beef strips to the marinade and season with salt and pepper. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
instructions.2: Bring rice and water to a boil in a saucepan over high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low and cover; simmer until rice is tender and liquid has been absorbed, 20 to 25 minutes.
instructions.3: Preheat the oven to 220 degrees C. Place 6 Korean stone bowls in the oven.
instructions.4: Combine shiitake mushrooms and 1/2 cup hot water in a small bowl; soak until pliable, about 10 minutes. Trim off and discard stems. Thinly slice caps and set aside.
instructions.5: Bring a saucepan of water to a boil. Add spinach to water just long enough to wilt leaves, then drain and pat dry. Set aside.
instructions.6: Combine cucumber and carrots in a bowl; season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
instructions.7: Preheat a wok over medium-high heat.
instructions.8: Cook and stir carrots and cucumbers in a small amount of sesame oil in the wok until softened. Remove from the wok and set aside. Add a small amount of sesame oil to the wok; cook and stir spinach in sesame oil for 1 to 2 minutes. Remove spinach from the wok and set aside. Add meat strips and marinade to the wok; cook, stirring frequently, until liquid reduces in volume, about 4 to 5 minutes.
instructions.9: Transfer the stone bowls from the oven to a suitable heat-resistant surface. Brush each bowl with sesame oil to coat. Divide rice into the bowls and gently pack to the bottom (the rice should sizzle as you arrange). Arrange cucumbers, carrots, bean sprouts, spinach, shiitake mushrooms, and beef mixture over each portion of rice.
instructions.10: Add one fried egg to each bowl, drizzle with 1 tablespoon sesame oil, and top with nori. Serve Kochujang sauce as a condiment.

w-kr-001.culturalNotes: Dol Sot Bibimbap is a traditional Korean dish served in hot stone bowls. The ingredients are mixed with rice before eating.

w-kr-002.title: Bibimbap

instructions.1: Cut the carrots into matchstick-sized strips.
instructions.2: Boil the strips in a covered pot of salted water for a few minutes. Drain.
instructions.3: Rinse the carrots with cold water until cool. Drain again, then put in a bowl.
instructions.4: Add the sesame oil, ground sesame seeds, grated garlic, and salt. Toss together with your fingers.

w-kr-002.culturalNotes: Bibimbap is a traditional Korean dish typically served with rice and a variety of vegetables.

w-kr-003.title: Bingsu with Sweet Red Beans

instructions.1: If using a special round container for the ice, fill it with water and put it in the freezer to make ice.
instructions.2: Open cans, clean berries, and prepare each of the toppings.
instructions.3: Slice strawberries.
instructions.4: Shave the ice into a large bowl that can hold all the ingredients.
instructions.5: Sprinkle the roasted grains powder on the ice using a small sieve.
instructions.6: Add berries and mini mochi rice cake.
instructions.7: Spoon the sweet red beans on top or on the side, then drizzle the sweetened condensed milk.

w-kr-003.culturalNotes: Bingsu is a traditional Korean dessert served in the summer, consisting of shaved ice with fruits and sweet toppings.

w-kr-004.title: Hobak Bokkeum (Stir-Fried Zucchini)

instructions.1: Cut the summer squash into 6 mm thick slices, then cut into equal sizes. If using Korean round squash, cut into quarters. If using common long zucchini, cut into half circles.
instructions.2: Chop the fermented shrimp until it is finely ground. When scooping out the shrimp from the jar, try to take out the shrimp but not the brine.
instructions.3: In a bowl, add the sliced squash and chopped fermented shrimp and mix gently. Let it sit for 30 minutes, turning over 2-3 times during this period.
instructions.4: While you wait, chop the garlic, fresh red chili pepper, and green onions.
instructions.5: In a frying pan over medium-high heat, sauté the garlic in perilla or sesame oil until it starts to bubble but not brown (less than a minute).
instructions.6: Add the squash and any liquid that has collected in the bowl to the frying pan, along with the water. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes over medium-high to medium heat until the zucchini is slightly crunchy but soft.
instructions.7: Right before turning off the heat, add the chopped green onions and sliced fresh red chili pepper (if using).
instructions.8: Transfer the stir-fried Hobak Bokkeum to a large plate or tray and spread it out to cool quickly. Sprinkle with sesame seeds. Cooling the bokkeum quickly helps to keep its vibrant green color.

w-kr-004.culturalNotes: Stir-fried bokkeum is a popular Korean side dish, typically served with warm rice.

w-kr-005.title: Crispy Zucchini Pancakes (Hobak Buchimgae)

instructions.1: Cut the Korean zucchini into 1/4 inch slices and then into matchsticks. One zucchini should make about 2 cups.
instructions.2: Peel and slice the onion into thin slices, similar thickness as the zucchini.
instructions.3: Sprinkle 1 teaspoon of sea salt over the zucchini sticks and toss them. Make sure the salt is evenly distributed. Leave them salted for 5-7 minutes.
instructions.4: Gently squeeze out excess water from the zucchini sticks.
instructions.5: In a large bowl, add the zucchini sticks, sliced onions, flour, water, and tempura mix. Mix gently until fully combined. The consistency should be like pancake batter or drinkable yogurt.
instructions.6: Heat a non-stick frying pan or cast iron pan on medium-high heat with about 1-2 tablespoons of oil.
instructions.7: Fry the pancake until the edges turn brown. This should take about 3 minutes on each side.
instructions.8: Flip the pancake when the bottom side edges turn golden brown.
instructions.9: Add more oil (1 tablespoon or more) after flipping the pancake.
instructions.10: When both sides are browned, move the pancake to a cutting board and cut it into bite-sized pieces.
instructions.11: Serve the pancake hot with a soy sauce and vinegar dipping sauce.

w-kr-005.culturalNotes: Hobak Buchimgae is a type of crispy Korean pancake made from zucchini. It is typically served as an appetizer or part of a breakfast meal.

w-kr-006.title: Budae-jjigae (Korean Army Base Stew)

instructions.1: Divide the fully cooked halal chicken luncheon meat into two piles on either side of a stock pot; layer the sausage, onion, and kimchi on top, leaving an empty space in the center of the pot.
instructions.2: Combine the Korean red pepper powder, gochujang, soy sauce, garlic, and black pepper in a small bowl; pour into the center of the pot. Sprinkle in the green onions and pour in the chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally until the flavors combine.
instructions.3: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the ramen noodles and cook, stirring until partially cooked and softened, about 2 minutes. Drain and transfer to the pot with the meat-kimchi mixture. Cook and stir until the ramen noodles are tender but firm to the bite, about 5 minutes. Top the stew with the cheese.

w-kr-006.culturalNotes: Budae-jjigae is a traditional Korean stew that originated in the post-Korean War era, using ingredients available from U.S. military bases.

w-kr-007.title: Fried Kelp Chips (Dasima Bugak)

instructions.1: Heat the vegetable oil in a deep frying pan or fryer.
instructions.2: While the oil is heating, wipe both sides of the kelp sheet with a wet towel to remove any extra salt residue.
instructions.3: Cut the kelp sheet into 1.5 x 1.5 inch squares using scissors.
instructions.4: Prepare a plate lined with paper towels or a fryer basket next to the fryer.
instructions.5: When the oil is heated enough (150°C/300°F), throw in a handful of kelp pieces and start frying. The kelp pieces should balloon or flower in just seconds. When they have floated to the top, leave them to fry a couple more seconds and using a spider or a fryer basket, take them out onto the prepared plate.
instructions.6: Once it’s cooled a little, sprinkle sugar generously on both sides.

w-kr-007.culturalNotes: Fried kelp chips (Dasima Bugak) are a popular snack in South Korea, typically served as an appetizer or light snack.

w-kr-008.title: Chong Gak Kimchi (Chong Gak Kimchi)

instructions.1: Wash the young radish and clean off excess dirt and roots. It works best if you scrape the outside with the edge of a knife. Clean the edges where the root part ends and the green stems start. Cut off any yellow leaves or stems and the outer greens if they look tough. Cut off the pointy root ends of the radish.
instructions.2: Get a large bowl. Salt the radish evenly by layering the radish and salting each layer as you go. Evenly spread out 1/4 cup of salt throughout. Sprinkle 1 cup of water on top of the salted radish. Gently turn the radish and salt water to make sure it gets an even coating of the salt and water. DO NOT handle the radish too much because it can bring out a grassy taste from the kimchi. Let it sit about 2 hours. In hot weather, 1 1/2 hrs should be sufficient. About halfway through, turn the radish once making sure every radish is salted properly.
instructions.3: Wash and clean green onions (about a handful or 2 bunches). Cut some of the thicker root ends in half and then cut green onions into 2 in long pieces.
instructions.4: Prepare the flour paste: Mix 1 Tbsp of flour with 1 cup of water until smooth.
instructions.5: Prepare the seasoning (yangnyum): Mix 3/4 cup of Korean red chili powder, 3 Tbsp of chopped garlic, 2 Tbsp of chopped ginger, 1/4 cup of fermented anchovy liquid, 1-2 Tbsp of sugar, and a pinch of salt (if needed).
instructions.6: Back to the pickled radishes: Drain the radish from the water and rinse it well with cold water. Cut the radish into 2 in long pieces. Place the radish in a large bowl and add the seasoning (yangnyum) and green onions. Mix the ingredients gently until well combined.
instructions.7: Place the kimchi in an airtight storage container. Let it sit at room temperature for 1-2 days before refrigerating. The kimchi can be stored in the refrigerator for up to a month.

w-kr-008.culturalNotes: Kimchi is a traditional Korean dish served as a side dish or with main meals. It is known for its sour and spicy flavor.

w-kr-009.title: Doenjang Jjigae (Korean Soybean Paste Stew)

instructions.1: Save 3 cups of rice water when rinsing rice.
instructions.2: Cut tofu and squash into squares, slice green onions and green chili pepper (if using), and chop garlic.
instructions.3: Add dried anchovies and kelp to rice water. Simmer on medium heat for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Discard anchovies and kelp.
instructions.5: Turn off heat and mix in doenjang. Smoosh it against the wall of your pot.
instructions.6: Turn heat to medium high and bring to a boil.
instructions.7: Add squash or zucchini squares. Boil for 5 minutes.
instructions.8: Add tofu squares. Boil for another 5 minutes.
instructions.9: Add green onions and chopped garlic. Boil for 3 more minutes.
instructions.10: Sprinkle with red chili pepper. Serve hot.

w-kr-009.culturalNotes: Doenjang Jjigae is a popular Korean dish, often served as part of a lunch or dinner meal.

w-kr-010.title: Dolsot Bibimbap

instructions.1: In a bowl, combine the meat with the marinade. Cover the bowl and leave it in the fridge while you are working on the other ingredients. When ready, add some cooking oil to a wok and cook the meat on medium high to high heat for about 3 to 5 minutes until thoroughly cooked.
instructions.2: Prepare the Korean cucumber side dish, fernbrake side dish, and sautéed bellflower root side dish according to the linked recipes. These can be prepared on a different day to save your bibimbap making time.
instructions.3: Sauté the carrots, zucchini, and mushrooms in a separate frying pan. Season them lightly with fine sea salt.
instructions.4: Mix the bibimbap sauce ingredients in a small bowl. Set aside.
instructions.5: Pan fry the eggs to your preference. (Sunny side up is a popular choice.)
instructions.6: Preheat an oven for 10 minutes at 220 C / 428 F. Once heated, place your stone bowl into the oven. Leave it there for 10 minutes. 10 minutes later, take it out. Add some sesame oil (about 1 Tbsp per medium size bowl) and brush it around.
instructions.7: Quickly assemble your bibimbap ingredients inside the hot stone bowl. First, lay down the rice and make sure you flatten it well. Then add the meat, assorted vegetables, and the egg on top of the rice.
instructions.8: Transfer the hot stone bowl onto the gas stove and cook it for 5 minutes over low heat. You will hear the rice crackling noise. Remove from the heat.
instructions.9: Pour the bibimbap sauce into the hot stone bowl and mix all the ingredients well. Serve.

w-kr-010.culturalNotes: Dolsot Bibimbap is a traditional Korean dish served in a hot stone bowl, which adds a special flavor and attractive appearance.

w-kr-011.title: Folded Kimbap (Kimbap Sandwich)

w-kr-011-i14.name: Korean pickled ssam radish or danmuji

instructions.1: Wash the rice and soak it for 30 minutes, then drain and cook according to the instructions.
instructions.2: Fry the eggs in a pan and slice them thinly.
instructions.3: Mix the chopped kimchi with sugar, sesame oil, and sesame seeds.
instructions.4: Heat a piece of nori on low heat until it becomes soft.
instructions.5: Place the rice on the nori sheet and spread it evenly.
instructions.6: Place the halal chicken luncheon meat slices, egg, kimchi mixture, cucumber, cheese, and pickled radish on the rice.
instructions.7: Roll the kimbap tightly using a bamboo mat.
instructions.8: Repeat the steps with the second nori sheet.
instructions.9: To prepare the tuna mayo folded kimbap, mix the tuna and mayonnaise in a bowl.
instructions.10: Place the tuna mayo mixture on a nori sheet and spread it evenly.
instructions.11: Place the perilla leaves, cucumber, cheese, and pickled radish on the tuna mayo mixture.
instructions.12: Roll the kimbap tightly using a bamboo mat.
instructions.13: Cut the kimbap into 2-3 cm pieces and serve hot.

w-kr-011.culturalNotes: Kimbap is a popular dish in South Korea, often served as a snack or quick lunch.

w-kr-012.title: Korean Glutinous Rice Ball Doughnuts

instructions.1: Mix the filling ingredients in a small bowl. If you want a smoother texture, blend or mash the sweetened red bean paste.
instructions.2: Sieve the sweet rice flour and self-raising flour into a large bowl. Add salt, melted butter, and hot water. Mix all the ingredients well and knead it to make one large dough.
instructions.3: Take the dough out onto a cutting board and divide it into smaller pieces to make mini round balls. While working through, cover the mini balls with plastic wrap to stop them from drying out.
instructions.4: Open up the dough by pressing the rolled balls with your thumbs. Add the filling mixture and close the dough. Repeat this until you use up the prepared ingredients.
instructions.5: Deep fry the donuts in a deep saucepan on medium-high heat until the dough is golden brown. Continuously roll the donuts while cooking to prevent sticking and improve shape. Place the cooked donuts onto a piece of oil-absorbing paper and cool down for 10 to 15 minutes.
instructions.6: Sprinkle the sugar onto the donuts or roll them on a plate of sugar. Alternatively, put the sugar into a plastic bag and add the donuts. Then while holding the top of the bag, shake the bag.
instructions.7: Enjoy the donuts.

w-kr-012.culturalNotes: Korean glutinous rice doughnuts are a popular sweet in Korea, known for their sweet flavor and soft texture.

w-kr-013.title: Cold Kimchi Noodle Soup (Kimchimari Guksu)

instructions.1: Boil a pot of water to cook the noodles.
instructions.2: Boil the egg using your favorite method. For hard-boiled eggs, add the eggs to a pot with cold water, set the heat to medium, and let it come to a boil slowly (so the egg doesn't crack), and let it cook for 10-12 minutes. Then transfer the eggs to an ice bath and peel after a few minutes. Slice the egg in half.
instructions.3: While the water is boiling, julienne the cucumber and set aside.
instructions.4: Cut the kimchi into small thin strips and season it with sugar, sesame seeds, and sesame oil (if you love sesame oil).
instructions.5: Cook the gluten-free noodles for 4-5 minutes, then rinse in cold water 2-3 times. Let it drain.
instructions.6: Prepare the broth - In a bowl, add chicken broth, water, and kimchi juice. Add vinegar, soy sauce, salt, sugar, and taste. You may want more vinegar or sugar. Keep it chilled in the fridge until serving time. To make it extra icy, put it in the freezer for about an hour to achieve a slushy consistency.
instructions.7: Assemble the soup - In a serving bowl, place the noodles, kimchi, cucumber, sliced egg, and roasted sea laver. Pour the chilled broth over the ingredients.

w-kr-013.culturalNotes: Kimchimari Guksu is a traditional Korean cold soup served in the summer. It is characterized by the tangy and spicy flavors of kimchi and vinegar, and is typically served as a light meal or lunch.

w-kr-014.title: Korean Pickles (Jangajji)

instructions.1: Mix soy sauce, vinegar, and sugar in a pot and let it come to a boil. When it boils, turn off the heat and let it sit.
instructions.2: Take a generous pinch of sea salt and clean the cucumbers by rubbing each one with salt.
instructions.3: Rinse the cucumbers with water and pat them dry. You can cut the cucumbers into bite-size pieces or keep them whole.
instructions.4: Wash the green chili peppers. Whole peppers can be used or can be cut into pieces. When using whole peppers, pierce them with a sharp skewer or toothpick.
instructions.5: Put the cucumbers and chili peppers into the jar. Pour the hot soy sauce mixture over the vegetables. The sauce should be quite hot to make the vegetables crunchy.
instructions.6: Find something to weigh the vegetables down and let it sit for 3 days at room temperature.
instructions.7: After 3 days, drain the liquid, boil it, and add it back to the jar while it is still hot. Leave it for 4 more days.

w-kr-014.culturalNotes: Jangajji is a type of Korean pickle typically prepared in the summer.

w-kr-015.title: Sujeonggwa (Korean Ginger Cinnamon Punch)

instructions.1: Peel the fresh ginger and slice it thinly.
instructions.2: Rinse the cinnamon sticks in water.
instructions.3: Prepare 2 pots that can hold 5 cups or more.
instructions.4: Add the sliced ginger to one pot with 5 cups of water. Bring to a boil and simmer for 20 minutes.
instructions.5: Add the cinnamon sticks to another pot with 5 cups of water. Bring to a boil and simmer for 20 minutes.
instructions.6: Strain the ginger water and cinnamon water to filter out any debris.
instructions.7: In a large pot or kettle, combine the ginger and cinnamon water. Add 1/2 cup of sugar and stir well.
instructions.8: Bring the mixture to a boil and simmer for 2-3 minutes. Let it cool. Chill in the refrigerator to serve cold.
instructions.9: If serving dried persimmons, soak the whole dried persimmon (including the stem) in the punch for at least 2 hours before serving so it will become soft at serving time. If you leave the dried persimmons in too long, they will start to disintegrate, so do not leave them in the liquid for too long. Also, not removing the stem will keep the fruit in whole shape.

w-kr-015.culturalNotes: Sujeonggwa is a traditional Korean drink served on special occasions and celebrations. It is known for its rich flavor of ginger, cinnamon, and dried persimmons.

w-kr-016.title: Korean Steamed Egg (Gyeran Jjim)

instructions.1: Chop the green onion and saewoojeot (fermented shrimp) and mix with sesame oil, sugar, and black pepper. Let it sit for a few minutes.
instructions.2: Whip the eggs in a bowl and add the water. Mix again.
instructions.3: Add the green onion and saewoojeot mixture to the eggs and mix well.
instructions.4: Pour the mixture into your favorite hot pot (such as a traditional Korean ttukbaegi) and place it on the stove over medium heat, covered for 7-8 minutes.
instructions.5: When the eggs are semi-cooked and still very watery, stir the mixture (bring the bottom to the top) to ensure even cooking. Cover again.
instructions.6: Turn the heat to low. Finish cooking for another 3 minutes.
instructions.7: Cook a little more if you like the bottom to be a little burnt, but not more than 1-2 minutes.
instructions.8: Sprinkle more black pepper, red chili powder (optional), and chopped green onion as garnish.

w-kr-016.culturalNotes: Korean steamed egg (Gyeran Jjim) is a traditional dish often served during family gatherings and celebrations in Korea.

w-kr-017.title: Jjapaguri

w-kr-017-i2.name: Neoguri (Korean instant spicy seafood udon noodles)

w-kr-017-i4.name: dried vegetable flakes from both packets

w-kr-017-i6.name: 1/3 packet of Neoguri powder soup sauce

instructions.1: Boil the water in a pot on medium high heat.
instructions.2: Once the water is boiling, add the Jjapaghetti and Neoguri noodles and the dried vegetable flakes from both packets.
instructions.3: Boil until the noodles are cooked, about 2-3 minutes. During this time, mix the noodles well by lifting and dropping them a couple of times.
instructions.4: Drain the water but leave about 6 tablespoons of water. Then add the full packet of Jjapaghetti powder soup sauce, 1/3 packet of Neoguri powder soup sauce, and olive oil. Mix well.
instructions.5: Serve hot.

w-kr-017.culturalNotes: Jjapaguri is a popular dish in South Korea, combining Jjapaghetti and Neoguri noodles to create a spicy and delicious meal.

w-kr-018.title: Korean Potato Side Dish (Gamja Jorim)

instructions.1: Rinse the potatoes. If using thick-skinned potatoes, peel and cut them into cubes.
instructions.2: Place the potatoes in a pot with enough water to fully cover them. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium and cook for about 10 minutes. Drain the potatoes.
instructions.3: Return the potatoes to the pot and add 2 cups of water, 3 tablespoons of soy sauce, sugar, vegetable oil, and the dried shiitake mushroom (if using). Bring to a boil, then simmer, covered, for about 30 minutes or until the liquid has reduced to one-third.
instructions.4: Uncover the pot, add 2 tablespoons of maple syrup. Continue to cook until the liquid has almost completely reduced. Taste and add more soy sauce if desired (up to 1 teaspoon).
instructions.5: Stir the potatoes for a few more minutes. Finish the dish with a swirl of sesame oil and a sprinkling of sesame seeds.

w-kr-018.culturalNotes: Gamja Jorim is a traditional Korean side dish, typically served with rice.

w-kr-019.title: Quick Kimchi

instructions.1: Rinse the napa cabbage well and cut an 'X' into the root end, going about 3 inches deep.
instructions.2: Pull apart at the 'X' to easily divide the cabbage into four equal segments.
instructions.3: Cut away the tough core and chop the cabbage into bite-sized pieces. Place in a large bowl, sprinkle with salt, and let sit for 2-3 hours, tossing occasionally.
instructions.4: While the cabbage is sitting, grate the ginger and garlic and cut the green onion into large pieces.
instructions.5: Measure out the red pepper powder and shrimp paste. You could easily double the red pepper for a fiery hot kimchi.
instructions.6: Drain the cabbage, pressing it through a colander, and return it to the mixing bowl. Stir together with the rest of the ingredients until evenly distributed.
instructions.7: Place the kimchi in an airtight container and let it sit on the counter for 2-3 days.
instructions.8: Everything will soften up, the juices will release, and it’ll be ready for nibbling. Refrigerate and use as desired. The kimchi will keep for a couple of weeks in the refrigerator.

w-kr-019.culturalNotes: Kimchi is a traditional Korean dish served with most meals. It is typically made from napa cabbage, green onions, garlic, and ginger.

w-kr-020.title: Korean Spicy Cold Noodles (Bibim Guksu)

instructions.1: Cook the thin dry Korean noodles in 5 cups of water until tender, then drain and rinse with cold water.
instructions.2: Peel the egg and slice it thinly.
instructions.3: In a small bowl, mix the grated apple, grated onion, minced garlic, rice vinegar, gochujang, gochukaru, soy sauce, sugar, honey, sesame oil, and soup soy sauce.
instructions.4: In another bowl, mix the sliced Korean radish, Korean sea salt, rice vinegar, and sugar.
instructions.5: In a serving bowl, place the noodles, then add the sliced egg, bibim sauce, sliced vegetables, and kimchi.
instructions.6: Gently toss the ingredients until well combined.
instructions.7: Serve the dish cold, garnished with red leaf lettuce and perilla leaves.

w-kr-020.culturalNotes: Bibim Guksu is a popular dish in Korea, typically served in the summer to enjoy its refreshing coolness.

w-kr-021.title: Pickled Yellow Radish (Danmuji) - Korean Style

instructions.1: Clean and sanitize the pickling jar by washing it with soap, rinsing it, and boiling it in a pot of hot water. If you are going to store it in the fridge, you can skip the boiling step and just use a dishwasher to clean the jar.
instructions.2: Clean the Korean radish (Mu) and brush the outer skin with a vegetable brush if the radish is fresh and clean enough to use the skin. If the skin is blemished or has black spots, it's best to peel the skin.
instructions.3: Cut the radish into 1/4 inch thick slices or into logs that will fit into the jar.
instructions.4: In a small pot, add 250 ml of water, 1/2 cup of sugar, 1 Tbsp of Korean sea salt, and 1/4 cup of rice vinegar to make the pickling juice.
instructions.5: Simmer the ingredients in the pot until all the seasoning has dissolved in the water.
instructions.6: While the pickling liquid is simmering, cut the radish into thin 1/4 inch slices or into chunks small enough to fit into your jar.
instructions.7: In the clean jar, pack in the radish and pour the hot pickling juice along with 3 pods of dried gardenia fruit (chija). Try to place the gardenia fruit well at the bottom for the whole jar to become evenly yellow.
instructions.8: Leave it in the jar for about a week until the radish starts to look a bit shriveled. Swirl it a couple of times so the gardenia fruit colors the radishes evenly.

w-kr-021.culturalNotes: Danmuji is a traditional Korean dish served as a side dish or with rice. It is known for its distinctive yellow color and sweet-sour taste.

w-kr-022.title: Tteok Mandu Guk (Rice Cake Soup with Dumplings)

w-kr-022-i9.name: 1/2 sheet gim nori, cut into thin strips

instructions.1: Cut the beef into thin bite-size pieces (1-1.5 inches).
instructions.2: In a medium pot, sauté the beef with 1 tablespoon of soup soy sauce until all the pieces turn brown. Pour in 5 cups of water and bring it to a boil. Skim off the foam. Reduce the heat to medium and continue to boil, covered, for 10 minutes.
instructions.3: You can add the dumplings to the soup along with the rice cakes in the next step. Another option is to cook the dumplings separately in the boiling water until the dumplings float to the top, and then add to the soup when the rice cakes are cooked. Or, line a steamer with a wet cheesecloth and then steam mandu for about 8 minutes (10 minutes if frozen).
instructions.4: Add the garlic and the rice cake slices to the boiling broth. Boil until the rice cakes turn very soft, usually about 5-8 minutes.
instructions.5: Drop the cooked dumplings and the scallion into the soup. Let the soup come to a boil again. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Ladle the steaming soup into individual bowls and garnish with the optional egg and gim strips.

w-kr-022.culturalNotes: Tteok Mandu Guk is a popular dish in South Korea, often served on special occasions.

w-kr-023.title: Brown Rice and Pumpkin Porridge (Hyunmi Danhobak Mium)

instructions.1: Wash the brown rice and soak it in water for 30 minutes. Drain the water after 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Wash, cut, and peel the pumpkin. Steam it in a boiling pot until it is cooked (20 to 25 minutes). It can be quicker if the pumpkin is chopped thinner and smaller.
instructions.3: Add the rice, steamed pumpkin, and water to a blender and blend for 1 to 2 minutes.
instructions.4: Pour the mixture into a small pot and bring it to a boil over high heat for 2 minutes. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
instructions.5: Sieve the boiled porridge. (Discard what is left on the sieve).
instructions.6: Cool it down for 10 to 20 minutes, then serve it (or distribute it among pre-portioned containers for later consumption).

w-kr-023.culturalNotes: This porridge is a traditional Korean dish served to newborns and patients to aid in their recovery.

w-kr-024.title: Korean Seaweed Soup (Miyeok Guk)

w-kr-024-i2.name: beef
w-kr-024-i2.standardAmount: 120 g (4.2 ounces), sliced into smaller pieces

instructions.1: Soak the dried seaweed in cold water for 5 to 10 minutes until it expands. Drain the water and rinse the seaweed a couple of times in running water. Drain and squeeze out the water. If you’re using non pre-cut dried seaweed, cut it with scissors into pieces about the size of your little finger. Set it aside.
instructions.2: Combine the sliced beef with the salt and black pepper in a small bowl. Mix them well and set aside until needed.
instructions.3: Preheat a medium pot over medium heat for about 20 seconds. Add the sesame oil, seaweed, and beef. Stir them well until the beef is partly cooked (about 2 minutes).
instructions.4: Add the soy sauce, garlic, and water. Cover the pot and boil over medium to medium-high heat until the meat is fully cooked (10 to 15 minutes). Adjust the taste with more salt if needed.
instructions.5: Serve the soup warm with a bowl of steamed rice and other Korean side dishes.

w-kr-024.culturalNotes: Korean seaweed soup (Miyeok Guk) is a traditional dish served on special occasions, especially on a child's birthday.

w-kr-025.title: Naengmyeon (Korean Cold Noodle Soup)

instructions.1: Make the beef broth: Place the beef, garlic, ginger, onion, and water in a pot. Simmer for two hours. Strain the broth and add the Korean soup soy sauce, sea salt, cucumber pickle liquid, and radish pickle liquid. Let it cool.
instructions.2: Pickle the cucumber: Slice the cucumber thinly and add the salt, rice vinegar, and sugar. Mix well and let it sit for 10 minutes.
instructions.3: Pickle the radish: Slice the radish thinly and add the salt, rice vinegar, and sugar. Mix well and let it sit for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Boil the eggs: Place the eggs in boiling water for 10 minutes. Rinse with cold water and peel them.
instructions.5: Peel and slice the Asian pear: Peel the Asian pear and slice it thinly.
instructions.6: Cook the noodles: Boil water in a pot and add the noodles. Boil for 5 minutes or according to package instructions. Drain the noodles and rinse with cold water.
instructions.7: Serve the naengmyeon: Place the noodles in serving bowls, add the cold broth, pickled cucumber, pickled radish, boiled eggs, and slices of Asian pear.

w-kr-025.culturalNotes: Naengmyeon is a traditional Korean dish served in the summer to enjoy its refreshing coolness.

w-kr-026.title: Ssukgat Namul (Chrysanthemum Greens)

instructions.1: Start boiling 6 cups of water with 1 tsp of salt.
instructions.2: Wash and clean the chrysanthemum greens in water and drain.
instructions.3: Cut the bottom stem part into 2-inch lengths and the upper leafy parts into 4-5 inch lengths.
instructions.4: Chop the green onions and prepare an ice bath (a bowl of cold water + a bowl of ice) to put the blanched chrysanthemum leaves in.
instructions.5: Once the water starts boiling in the pot, add just the stem parts first and cook for 1 minute or so. Then add the rest of the leaves and cook for another 1-2 minutes until the thickest stems are cooked.
instructions.6: When it's cooked, quickly remove the pot from heat and transfer the cooked chrysanthemum leaves into the ice bath. Let it cool then remove the leaves from the ice bath and put into a colander.
instructions.7: Then take a handful of it between your hands and squeeze out excess water from the cooked greens. Gently squeeze but don't wring it totally out.
instructions.8: In a bowl, add the balls of squeezed greens and loosen them so the leaves are loosely separated. Now, add the green onions and seasonings - Guk Ganjang, sea salt, sesame seeds, and sesame oil. Use your hands (use gloves if you want) to gently massage all the seasonings into the greens. Once it's all nicely mixed, taste and adjust if necessary.
instructions.9: Serve at room temperature or cold from the fridge with any Korean dish.

w-kr-026.culturalNotes: Ssukgat Namul is a traditional Korean side dish served with many Korean dishes. It is known for its fresh flavor and slightly crunchy texture.

w-kr-027.title: Korean Radish Salad (Moosaengche)

instructions.1: Wash and peel the Korean radish.
instructions.2: Julienne the radish to make about 6 cups.
instructions.3: Put the julienned radish into a large bowl and sprinkle with sea salt. Toss the radish pieces to distribute the salt evenly.
instructions.4: Add the rice vinegar, sugar, and Korean red pepper powder. You can add more or less to taste.

w-kr-027.culturalNotes: This Korean radish salad, known as Moosaengche, is served as an appetizer in Korean meals.

w-kr-028.title: Ssamjang

w-kr-028-i8.name: walnuts (or your choice of nuts and seeds)

w-kr-028-i9.name: apple, cored and cut into small pieces

instructions.1: Add all ingredients to a food processor and blend until smooth. This will take about 1 minute.
instructions.2: Transfer the sauce to a serving bowl.
instructions.3: Garnish with green onion and sesame seeds if desired.

w-kr-028.culturalNotes: Ssamjang is a traditional Korean sauce used as a filling for fresh vegetables or grilled meats.

w-kr-029.title: Sujebi (Korean Hand-Pulled Noodle Soup)

w-kr-029-i3.name: water
w-kr-029-i3.standardAmount: 160 ml (add 1-2 tsp more if you didn't exact weigh your flour)

w-kr-029-i7.name: Korean sea salt
w-kr-029-i7.standardAmount: 1.5 tsp (use less if it's not Korean sea salt, also use 1 tsp if using yangnyeomjang later)

w-kr-029-i8.name: Korean soup soy sauce (guk ganjang)
w-kr-029-i8.standardAmount: 1.25 tsp (reduce to 1 tsp if using yangnyeomjang)

w-kr-029-i16.name: red chili pepper (chopped)
w-kr-029-i16.standardAmount: 2 tsp (substitute shishito peppers (double amount) if you want mild sauce, adjust to your spice level)

instructions.1: Prepare the dough: In a large bowl, mix the flour and salt. Gradually add the water and knead until the dough is smooth. Cover the dough and let it rest for 15 minutes.
instructions.2: Prepare the broth: In a large pot, bring 6 cups of water to a boil over medium heat. Add the dried anchovies and dried kelp, and simmer for 20 minutes. Strain the broth and remove the anchovies and kelp.
instructions.3: Prepare the vegetables: Cut the potato, yellow onion, and Korean aehobak or Italian zucchini into small cubes. Slice the green onions thinly.
instructions.4: Prepare the sauce (optional): In a small bowl, mix the minced garlic, regular soy sauce, Korean red chili powder, chopped red chili pepper, rice vinegar, oil, sugar, black pepper, and sesame seeds.
instructions.5: Prepare the soup: In a large pot, bring the broth to a boil. Add the potato, yellow onion, and Korean aehobak or Italian zucchini, and simmer for 10 minutes. Add the Korean sea salt and Korean soup soy sauce, and stir well.
instructions.6: Prepare the noodles: Cut the dough into small pieces, then stretch them between your hands to form the noodles. Add the noodles to the soup and simmer for 5 minutes.
instructions.7: Serve the soup: Ladle the soup into serving bowls, garnish with chopped green onions and the sauce (if prepared), and serve hot.

w-kr-029.culturalNotes: Sujebi is a traditional Korean soup made with hand-pulled noodles and vegetables. It is typically served in a large bowl and contains a rich, flavorful broth.

w-kr-030.title: Sundubu-jjigae (Korean Spicy Soft Tofu Stew)

w-kr-030-i8.name: dried kelp and dried anchovy stock

instructions.1: Start heating the pot on the stove over medium low heat and add the chili oil, chili powder, and garlic. Stir them well for about 1 min. Make sure not to burn the chili powder.
instructions.2: Add the clams and shrimps and stir quickly to coat them with the chili sauce. Add the fish sauce and soy sauce then stir.
instructions.3: Add the dried kelp and anchovy stock and boil it on medium-high heat until it starts to boil rapidly (2 to 3 mins).
instructions.4: Add the tofu, mushrooms, and egg and cook them for another 2 to 3 mins. Season with salt, if required.
instructions.5: Top up with the green onion, black pepper, and sesame oil. Serve hot with Korean rice and side dishes (banchan).

w-kr-030.culturalNotes: Sundubu-jjigae is a traditional Korean stew often served in a hot iron pot, and it is an important part of Korean cuisine.

w-kr-031.title: Tteokbokki

instructions.1: Make Kelp broth - soak dried kelp (Dasima or Kombu) in hot water for at least 10 minutes. Using plain water is okay but it won't be as flavorful.
instructions.2: Prepare Rice Cakes - If you have fresh or refrigerated rice cakes, just pull them apart so they are all separated. If your tteok is frozen, defrost by soaking it in cold water for a few minutes and then drain.
instructions.3: Pour kelp broth (or water) into a pan. Add tteok (rice cakes) and turn heat on medium high and bring to boil.
instructions.4: Add Tteokbokki Sauce - you can premix the sauce in a bowl first or you can just add Gochujang, sugar, soy sauce, garlic powder or chopped garlic directly and mix in the pan.
instructions.5: Once it starts to boil, lower heat to simmer and let it reduce for 10-13 minutes, depending on how thick you want the sauce to be.
instructions.6: Sprinkle some chopped green onions, sesame seeds, and a swirl of sesame oil (if desired). Enjoy!

w-kr-031.culturalNotes: Tteokbokki is a popular dish in South Korea, served as a snack or main meal. It is known for its spicy and sweet flavor.

w-kr-032.title: Korean Rice Cake Soup (Tteokguk)

instructions.1: If using frozen rice cakes, soak them in water for 10 minutes and drain. If using fresh rice cakes, rinse them quickly with water and drain.
instructions.2: Cut the onion in half and use half of it (not cut) for the broth. Slice the remaining half into thin slices to be added later.
instructions.3: Peel the garlic cloves and use some of them whole for the broth and chop the rest.
instructions.4: Add the beef, the uncut half of the onion, and the water to the Instant Pot. Close the lid and set the valve to sealing. Set the Instant Pot to the Soup setting and cook for 20 minutes.
instructions.5: After the cooking time, carefully release the pressure. Add the rice cakes, sliced onion, chopped garlic, soy sauce, sea salt, sugar, and black pepper. Mix the ingredients well.
instructions.6: Re-set the Instant Pot to the Soup setting for 10 minutes.
instructions.7: After the cooking time, carefully release the pressure. Add the sliced green onions, roasted seaweed, and beaten egg. Gently mix the ingredients.
instructions.8: Serve the soup hot, garnished with roasted seaweed and sliced green onions.

w-kr-032.culturalNotes: Korean Rice Cake Soup (tteokguk) is a traditional dish served on Korean New Year's Day.

w-kr-033.title: Yukgaejang - Korean Spicy Beef Soup

instructions.1: Soak the beef brisket in cold water for 5-10 minutes to draw out the blood, then rinse it well.
instructions.2: Peel the onion and garlic cloves.
instructions.3: In the Instant Pot or pressure cooker, add water, beef brisket, whole onion, and whole garlic cloves.
instructions.4: Cover the pot and select the Meat/Stew function and set the time to 30 minutes.
instructions.5: After the time is up, remove the beef brisket and cut it into small pieces.
instructions.6: In a bowl, mix the Korean red chili pepper, Korean Soup Soy Sauce, sea salt, Gochujang, sugar, chopped garlic, garlic powder, and ground black pepper.
instructions.7: Return the beef to the pot and add the spice mixture.
instructions.8: Add the green onions, mung bean sprouts, eggs, and Korean leek.
instructions.9: Re-cover the pot and cook for 10 minutes on low pressure.
instructions.10: After the time is up, remove the pot from heat and add the crushed sesame seeds and sesame oil.
instructions.11: Serve the soup hot with rice if desired.

w-kr-033.culturalNotes: Yukgaejang is a traditional Korean spicy beef soup, often served on special occasions and during the winter.
